name: גַּבְרִיאֵל
gloss: man of God; or God is my mighty one
summary: The angel sent to Daniel to make him understand the vision (Dan 8:16) and the seventy sevens (Dan 9:21–27), and to Zechariah and to Mary, “Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God” (Luk 1:19, 26). Daniel saw him standing before him “as the appearance of a גָּבֶר” and calls him “the man Gabriel” (Dan 8:15; 9:21): angels appear as men, but are God's messengers, “mighty in strength, that do his word” (Psa 103:20). The name joins אֵל to גֶּבֶר “man” (“man of God”) or to the root's “mighty one” with “my” (“God is my mighty one”); scripture does not explain it, but Dan 8:15–16 sets the name beside the word גֶּבֶר.

evidence.note: “There stood before me as the appearance of a גָּבֶר. And I heard a man's voice … which called and said, גַּבְרִיאֵל, make this one understand the vision.”
“The man (וְהָאִישׁ) גַּבְרִיאֵל, whom I had seen in the vision at the beginning.”
“I am Gabriel, who stands in the presence of God, and I was sent to speak to you.” The Peshitta spells it גַּבְרִיאֵיל.
His angels, “גִּבֹּרֵי כֹחַ, that do his word”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 374, art. جبر, جَبْرَئِيلُ (n4946)
evidence.note: Arabic tradition explains the name from جَبْرٌ “man” or “servant” and إِيلٌ “God”.
